description: A granular oscillator after Barry Truax's GSX system: up to twenty streams each firing short windowed grains, from a pitched tone to a formless cloud

params.text: Sets the centre frequency of the grains, 50Hz to 2000Hz
Sets how many grain generators run at once, 1 to 20; more of them makes the texture smoother and fewer lets single grains be heard
Sets the waveform inside each grain, morphing from sine through triangle and sawtooth to square
Sets how far a grain's frequency can fall either side of the centre, 0 to 500Hz
Sets how long each grain lasts, 1ms to 100ms
Sets the time between grains directly, 0.1ms to 200ms, in place of the density figure
Sets how many grains each stream fires per second, 1 to 1000
Sets how much the grain timing, frequency, length and placement are randomised, from regular spacing at one end of the travel to fully scattered at the other
Sets how wide across the stereo pair the grains are thrown, from all at the centre to the full width

inputs.text: Moves the centre frequency a volt per octave
Changes the stream count, added to the streams knob at two streams per volt and clamped to 1 to 20
Changes the grain waveform, added to the shape knob at a fifth per volt and clamped to the knob's travel
Changes the frequency deviation, added to the range knob at 100Hz per volt and clamped to 0 to 500Hz
Changes the grain length, added to the duration knob at 20ms per volt and clamped to 1ms to 100ms
Changes the time between grains, added to the delay knob at 40ms per volt and clamped to 0.1ms to 200ms
Changes the grain rate, added to the density knob at 200 grains per second per volt and clamped to 1 to 1000
Changes how much the grain stream is randomised, added to the variation knob at a fifth per volt and clamped to the knob's travel
Changes the stereo width, added to the spread knob at a fifth per volt and clamped to the knob's travel
Sets the output level, 0-5V for silence to full; with nothing patched the module runs at full level

outputs.text: The left side of the grain cloud
The right side of the grain cloud

notes: the module makes sound as soon as it is placed: the streams fire continuously and there is no gate or trigger to start them
the output is scaled by one over the square root of half the number of grains sounding, so the level holds steady as the density is raised
